open_points.subject: bindings.check_installed_instances manifest validation
open_points.text: “an unreadable record, or one failing a check of the record itself (A08 rule 5), fails at its service”
open_points.question: With no operation name or proposed ports supplied at startup, exactly which A08 rule 5 checks are applied, and are they applied to every capability or only to the service-record structure?
options: Check only service-level structure: readable JSON, matching service field, capabilities present and unique names
Validate every capability entry’s record-only fields, including effect class, exposure and idempotency-key syntax
Do not validate capabilities at startup; check only headers of the selected instance
open_points.default_guess: Validate the service-level structure and every capability’s record-only fields, but omit all checks requiring a selected operation or proposed ports.

open_points.subject: installation service identifiers
open_points.text: “no service twice among the selected instances or among the credentials”
open_points.question: Must service identifiers appearing in installation selections and credentials satisfy SERVICE_ID_PATTERN, and which operation refuses an invalid configured identifier before any manifest path is built?
options: load_installation validates every configured service identifier
check_installed_instances validates identifiers only when it examines a credentialed service
Configured service identifiers are not validated unless later supplied by an MCP binding request
open_points.default_guess: Validate every configured service identifier in load_installation before any manifest access.

open_points.subject: store.read_records relations naming embedded elements
open_points.text: “The record a relation names — every one of them — must exist” versus “from an existing record, an empty answer is a result” and “a well-formed element with no record yet is a result — not reached, or empty — never a refusal.”
open_points.question: For relations such as executions, approvals or attempts of an element, and active grant of a flow-version node, does store validate that the embedded node or mapped element exists, or trust the caller and return an empty relation when no matching records exist?
options: Validate only actual top-level records such as the run or flow version, and trust embedded node and element facts
Inspect the pinned graph and validate the node and map index inside store
Treat any element with no related record as unknown_reference
open_points.default_guess: Validate only named top-level records and trust the embedded node or element supplied by the owning module; return an empty result when it has no related records.

open_points.subject: get_repair_view execution page for a slot with no implementations
open_points.text: “through store.page_records the latest NodeExecutions of the slot's implementations” while page_records permits an in-set filter only for “a non-empty set of values”
open_points.question: What does get_repair_view do when the slot has no implementations and therefore its executed_implementation filter set is empty?
options: Return an empty execution page without calling store.page_records
Permit an empty in-set filter for this operation
Refuse the repair view as invalid_request
open_points.default_guess: Return an empty execution page with no continuation token without calling store.page_records.

open_points.subject: functions.roll_back_slot naming the current implementation
open_points.text: “Requires an admitted verdict over the current corpus; runs no admission; naming the current one records nothing”
open_points.question: If corpus growth left the currently active implementation without an admitted verdict over the current corpus, does roll_back_slot naming that same current implementation return its activation unchanged or refuse it for lacking the verdict?
options: Require the current-corpus admitted verdict even for the current implementation
Treat naming the current implementation as an idempotent no-op before checking its verdict
open_points.default_guess: Require an admitted verdict over the current corpus, even when the named implementation is already current.

open_points.subject: store.open_store privacy check
open_points.text: “private directory” and “The directory and everything in it are private to the kernel's user”
open_points.question: What exact ownership and permission conditions define a private data directory and private existing contents for the open_store start check?
options: Kernel-user ownership and no permissions for group or others on every directory and file
Only the data-directory root must be kernel-user-owned with no group or other permissions
Require exact modes such as 0700 for directories and 0600 for files
open_points.default_guess: Require kernel-user ownership and no group or other permission bits on the root and every existing entry, without requiring exact owner permission bits.

open_points.subject: runs.continue_after_approval send guarantee
open_points.text: “An approved effect is sent in this request” versus “after an approval the element is reached again” and the rules that a pre-send check may fail or a changed request digest may require another approval
open_points.question: Does approving guarantee that an HTTP request leaves the kernel during the same call, or does the call merely reach the element again and possibly end in operation_failed or another owner_approval wait without sending?
options: Rebuild and recheck; send only if pre-send checks pass and the approval or another authority covers the rebuilt request
Send the request that was previewed without rerunning pre-send checks
Refuse the approval decision itself when the request can no longer be sent exactly as approved
open_points.default_guess: Record the approval, rebuild and recheck the request, and send only when current checks and authority permit it; otherwise return the resulting failure or wait.
